question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}xy, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{2}{3},$ find $\text{E}[X+Y].$
question.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[Y].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[X].$

The marginal density function for $X$ when $0\le x\le 2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}xy\,\text{d}y \\  & =x{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{x}{2}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot \frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(8-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X+Y] & =\text{E}[X]+\text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{6}{3} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
